topic: The Bridge Between Slopes and Areas: Understanding the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
target_audience: High school seniors or early university students

sections.title: Introduction: The Inverse Relationship
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
Meet Dash the Cheetah, our fast friend.
Can we find distance if we only know speed?
animations: 1. Dash the Cheetah runs across; label position $P(t)$ in #ADD8E6.
2. A needle-like gauge appears for speed $v(t) = P'(t)$ in #FFD700.
3. A question mark appears between 'Speed' and 'Total Distance'.

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: Slopes and Areas
lecture_lines: Derivative measures the slope of a tangent line.
Integral calculates the signed area under a curve.
For f(x)=2x, the area grows as x increases.
animations: 1. Draw $f(x)=2x$ in #90EE90; tangent line shows constant slope 2.
2. Shade area under $f(x)=2x$ from 0 to $x$ in #FFB6C1.
3. Display labels 'Slope=Derivative' and 'Area=Integral' in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Accumulation Function
lecture_lines: Let A(x) be the area from a to x.
This is the "Area-so-far" or accumulation function.
Like a snowblower, A(x) collects area as it moves.
The total area depends on the moving point x.
And it depends on the height f(t) at each spot.
animations: 1. Curve $f(t)$ in #F0E68C; mark 'a' and moving 'x'.
2. Vertical line at 'x' moves right; area $A(x)$ fills #87CEFA.
3. Show $A(x) = \int_a^x f(t) dt$ in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The 'Aha!' Moment: The Rate of Area Growth
lecture_lines: How fast does the area A(x) actually grow?
Add a tiny sliver of width dx at x.
The extra area is roughly height f(x) times dx.
So the rate of change A'(x) is just f(x).
This links the derivative directly back to the function.
animations: 1. Zoom in on the boundary of $A(x)$ at position $x$.
2. Add a tiny sliver of width $\Delta x$ in #FFA07A.
3. Label the sliver height as $f(x)$ in #F0E68C.
4. Show the sliver area $\Delta A \approx f(x) \cdot \Delta x$.
5. Scale $\Delta x \to 0$ to show $A'(x) = f(x)$ in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Application: Speedometers and Odometers
lecture_lines: Your car's speedometer shows the derivative, velocity.
The odometer tracks the integral, the total distance.
Integrating velocity over time gives the change in distance.
We calculate this by evaluating the antiderivative at endpoints.
This is the Fundamental Theorem in the real world.
animations: 1. Car dashboard: Speedometer needle moves in #FFD700.
2. Odometer numbers tick up in #FFFFFF.
3. Labels 'Speedometer=$v(t)$' and 'Odometer=$\int v(t) dt$' appear.
4. Plot $v(t)$; shade the area under the curve #87CEFA.
5. Highlight odometer change matching the shaded area value.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Differentiation breaks down a function into its slopes.
Integration builds up a function from its area.
The Fundamental Theorem is the bridge between them.
animations: 1. Left: Derivative $\frac{d}{dx}$ finds slope on a curve.
2. Right: Integral $\int$ builds up area under a curve.
3. 'Fundamental Theorem' bridge connects them in #E0FFFF.
